questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain zero profit in long-run equilibrium
questions.stem: A marine biologist's tank competitive market has free entry; what happens to economic profit in the long run?

answer.exemplar: Free entry and exit drive economic profit to zero in the long run. If profit is positive, entry increases supply and lowers price; if negative, exit raises price. Equilibrium has zero economic profit.

questions.explanation: Entry and exit adjust supply until price equals minimum average total cost, yielding zero economic profit in the long run.
questions.hint: Entry and exit drive profit to zero.

questions.stem: A marine biologist's tank monopolist has marginal revenue 14 and marginal cost 14 at 18 units; what output maximises profit?

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Marginal revenue from a demand elasticity
questions.learningObjective: Compute marginal revenue from elasticity
questions.stem: A marine biologist's tank monopolist charges price 30 with demand elasticity -3; what is marginal revenue?
questions.explanation: Marginal revenue equals price times (1 + 1/elasticity). With price 30 and elasticity -3, MR = 30*(1 - 1/3) = 20.
questions.hint: Apply MR = P(1+1/E).
